greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who calls us to a life of interior truth and freedom, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you look past our outward appearances to the truth of our hearts, Lord have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you call us to the freedom of the children of God, Christ have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you invite us to share in your divine light and love, Lord have mercy.
psalm_response: Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
homily:
We often find ourselves living in the world of the 'outside.' We are preoccupied with the surfaces of things—the way a room is arranged, the way we present ourselves to our neighbors, the way our lives look from the sidewalk. We spend so much energy polishing the dish, making sure the exterior is bright and orderly, hoping that if the outside is right, then the inside will surely follow. But today, in the Gospel of Luke, Jesus sits at the table of a Pharisee and shatters that illusion. He looks right through the ritual hand-washing, right through the careful observance of the law, and he speaks to the heart. 'Did not the maker of the outside also make the inside?' he asks. It is a question that invites us to stop tending to the surface and start tending to the soul.

Imagine a beautifully crafted instrument—a violin, perhaps, or a complex piece of code written by a brilliant mind. The casing might be polished to a mirror finish, but if the strings inside are slack, or if the logic within the lines of code is broken, the beauty of the object is lost. Jesus is telling us that God is not interested in the polish of our reputation or the precision of our performance. He is interested in the interior. He is interested in the secret places where we hold our grief, our dreams, and our deepest loves. He is the Maker of both, and he is calling us to let the inside match the outside: to be as authentic in our hidden sorrow as we are in our public life.

This is the same freedom that St. Paul writes about to the Galatians. He says, 'For freedom Christ set us free; so stand firm and do not submit again to the yoke of slavery.' The yoke Paul speaks of is the burden of trying to earn our worth through outward signs—through circumcision, through rules, through checking boxes. But we are not saved by what we do; we are saved by who we are in Christ. We are set free from the exhausting need to prove ourselves. We are set free to simply be. And in that freedom, we find the capacity to love, not because it is a law, but because it is our nature.

Benjamin Vo lived with this kind of internal integrity. He was a boy who did not need to perform to be loved. Whether he was sitting in a bright red t-shirt on a summer evening, knees pulled up, chatting with his family, or standing in his NASA sweatshirt posing for a photo with his dad and brother, there was a natural, unforced quality to him. He was a boy who was comfortable in his own skin. He didn't live for the applause of the world; he lived for the connections of the heart. Think of that moment, so quiet and so profound, when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, he didn't need to tell anyone. The offer itself was the truth of his heart. It was a secret, interior movement of love. It was a sign that Benjamin understood, better than most adults, that our value is not in what we keep, but in what we are willing to offer.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has been a heavy companion. You remember the way Ben would come to you with his ideas, his plans, his gentle smile. You remember the way he would listen—truly listen—to the stories his dad would tell, finding joy in the simple, quiet connection of a father and son. That bond is not a thing of the past. It is a living, breathing reality. It is the 'Jerusalem above' that Paul speaks of. It is the place where all of our loves are gathered and kept safe, beyond the reach of time or change. You are a family of four, and that is a truth that death cannot touch, because it is anchored in the promise of the One who is the Resurrection and the Life.

Sometimes, the weight of a life that has been completed so early feels like an impossible burden. You look at the empty space where he should be, and you wonder how to keep going. You might even feel a flicker of guilt, a thought that maybe you should have done more, or seen more, or held him tighter. I want to lift that stone from your hearts today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the secret language of that love. You know that Ben is not gone; he has simply gone ahead to the place where all the 'con chim airlines' finally take flight. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity, his kindness, and his smile. When you sit down to code, or when you look up at the clouds, know that you are not doing it alone. You are a family of four, and that bond is stronger than death. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the brother who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share. You are a witness to the fact that love is the only thing that actually lasts.

Look at the Gospel again. Jesus says, 'But as to what is within, give alms, and behold, everything will be clean for you.' This is the secret of the Christian life. We cleanse the inside not by scrubbing it, but by giving it away. We give our love, we give our time, we give our attention to others. When we pour ourselves out, the interior of our soul becomes clear. We stop worrying about our own emptiness and start focusing on the needs of our brothers and sisters. That is why the Well of Love in Vietnam is such a powerful, living sign of Benjamin’s life. It is his love, still flowing. It is his kindness, still quenching the thirst of those who are far away. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow.

Do not be afraid of the silence, and do not be afraid of the ache. That ache is simply your love looking for a place to land. Let it land on the promise of the Resurrection. Let it land on the certainty that Benjamin is not in the past; he is in the future. He is at the destination, waiting for you to complete the journey. He is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion.

There is a profound freedom in realizing that we do not have to hold it all together. We do not have to be the ones who provide the answers. We are children of the freeborn woman. We are heirs to a kingdom that is not built by human hands, but by the grace of God. That grace is the 'bread' we need for the journey. It is the strength that comes when our own strength is gone. It is the peace that settles over us when we finally stop fighting the silence and start listening to the voice of the Father.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, that he may rest in the eternal light and peace of Christ, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, especially Benjamin’s family, that God may console them, strengthen their hearts, and give them the hope of the Resurrection, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
For freedom Christ set us free;
so stand firm and do not submit again to the yoke of slavery.It is I, Paul, who am telling you
that if you have yourselves circumcised,
Christ will be of no benefit to you.
Once again I declare to every man who has himself circumcised
that he is bound to observe the entire law.
You are separated from Christ,
you who are trying to be justified by law;
you have fallen from grace.
For through the Spirit, by faith, we await the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus,
neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything,
but only faith working through love.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (41a) Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
Let your mercy come to me, O LORD,
your salvation according to your promise.
R. Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
Take not the word of truth from my mouth,
for in your ordinances is my hope.
R. Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
And I will keep your law continually,
forever and ever.
R. Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
And I will walk at liberty,
because I seek your precepts.
R. Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
And I will delight in your commands, 
which I love.
R. Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.
And I will lift up my hands to your commands
and meditate on your statutes.
R. Let your mercy come to me, O Lord.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
After Jesus had spoken,
a Pharisee invited him to dine at his home.
He entered and reclined at table to eat.
The Pharisee was amazed to see
that he did not observe the prescribed washing before the meal.
The Lord said to him, “Oh you Pharisees!
Although you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish,
inside you are filled with plunder and evil.
You fools!
Did not the maker of the outside also make the inside?
But as to what is within, give alms,
and behold, everything will be clean for you.”

day: Tuesday of the Twenty-eighth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
